key_insight: In localized nonorthogonal flow representations, Reynolds stress is assembled from coupled velocity fluctuations, so additive component energies alone cannot capture its attribution.
engineering_relevance: Structure-based turbulence analysis should retain span overlap and cross covariance to avoid misleading attribution of turbulent momentum flux.
method: Represent JHTDB turbulence with a frozen solenoidal expansion of curl-lifted anisotropic Gaussian vorticity functions.
Map coefficient covariance to velocity stress through a fixed Biot–Savart operator.
Analyze principal-angle overlap and cross covariance, then compare with orthogonal Fourier and POD regroupings.
evidence_signal: In JHTDB homogeneous isotropic turbulence, 55% of sheet-associated directions overlap the tube-like family at a principal-cosine threshold of 0.95; shared-direction products carry 99.6% of covariance cancellation, and removing between-family covariance raises DNS-referenced stress error by factors of 53.6–87.
watch_item: Blob, sheet, and tube labels are representation-dependent; the findings do not establish unique physical attribution of Reynolds stress.
paper_title: Identifiability Limits of Reynolds-Stress Attribution in Localized Nonorthogonal Flow Representations
